clue.text: With green light to enter country, exercised rivalry around Syria's borders

definitions.text: With green light to enter country

indicators.note: around tells us the rivalry word wraps itself about the border letters

parts.note: to vie is to compete, so exercised rivalry is vied

indicators.note: the borders of the word Syria are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A news item about political rivalry in the Middle East, with talk of permission to enter a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes the outer letters S and A of Syria, and 'around' puts VIED round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport that has been visaed carries the stamp giving official permission to enter.

clue.text: Judge backing up leaderless faction — they're linked to Rebel Alliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, backing up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so reversed
leaderless means the faction word loses its first letter

parts.note: a side is a faction or team

explanation.surface: A judge supports a faction that has lost its leader, in a political feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' suits a down clue, where reversed letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Wars the Jedi knights fight alongside the Rebel Alliance against the Empire.

clue.text: Stokes's last over — look at that individual performance!

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Stokes's

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
lo is an old exclamation meaning look, behold

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator marvels at Ben Stokes's final over, a one-man show.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Stokes is an England cricketer; an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a performance given by one person alone, without any partners.

clue.text: Agitator ploughing Russian cash into Twitter's extremists

indicators.note: ploughing, paired with into further on, means the currency is driven in between other letters
into completes the ploughing instruction, saying where the currency goes
the extremists of Twitter are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser using Russian money to stir up extremists on Twitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' gives T and R, the outside letters of Twitter, and ROUBLE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who troubles others stirs up unrest, just as an agitator does.

clue.text: Backing for yellow vests securing popular gains

indicators.note: securing means the two outer letters hold the popular word between them
the backing for each word is its rear letter, so take the last letters of both

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Support for the French yellow-vest protesters wins favour with the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing for' gives W and S, the ends of yellow and vests; they enclose IN. The gilets jaunes were French protesters in yellow vests.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to gain it, so wins and gains are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: With pressure involved, running Tories' PR gets more difficult to handle

indicators.note: involved means the pressure letter is brought inside the jumbled letters
running is taken in the sense of run riot, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Under pressure, the Conservatives' public relations campaign gets harder to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges TORIESPR to STROPIER, and 'involved' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stroppy is bad-tempered and awkward, so stroppier means harder to manage.

clue.text: It's abrasive when football manager meets directors

parts.note: Unai Emery was the manager of Arsenal football club in 2019
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A football club's manager meeting the directors is a rough encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrasive' hints at a heated boardroom row, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board is a nail file coated with gritty abrasive powder.

clue.text: Risqué cracks on Conservative right-winger demanding title

indicators.note: cracks means the word Risqué is broken up and its letters reassembled
the right wing of a word written across is its last letter, so the end of Conservative

explanation.surface: A right-wing Tory insists on a title after making near-the-knuckle jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' rearranges RISQUE to ESQUIR; 'right-winger' adds E, the last letter of Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire is a courtesy title, written as Esq. after a man's name.

clue.text: Aspiring professional party needs skill to face both ways to preserve union

indicators.note: to preserve means the two-way letters keep the union letter safe between them
to face is to turn round, so the leftover pair is set down backwards
needs is read as lacks, so the skill word is taken away from party

parts.note: the word party is taken as written
art is a skill or craft, as in the art of conversation
both ways says the same leftover pair from party also appears facing forwards, a second copy

explanation.surface: A political party must learn to look both ways to keep a union together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is read as lacks. 'face both ways' sets the two leftover letters down once backwards ('face') and once forwards ('both ways'), and 'to preserve' holds the union letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppy, a young urban professional, is an ambitious, upwardly mobile career type.

clue.text: Barnet seat Conservative's held

indicators.note: held is read as held off or kept out, so the Conservative letter is removed

parts.note: a chair is a seat
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: The Chipping Barnet parliamentary seat has been held by the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London constituency, but here it is rhyming slang: Barnet Fair means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang Barnet, short for Barnet Fair, stands for the stuff on your head.

clue.text: 'Money for nothing' conceals question — Ukraine's chief getting something in return?

indicators.note: conceals means the money-for-nothing letters hide the question and Ukraine letters within

parts.note: a quid is a pound, slang for money
pro means for, in favour of
O is the zero of nothing

indicators.note: the chief of Ukraine is its first letter

explanation.surface: A line on Trump's impeachment: 'money for nothing' hides questions about Ukraine's president and a favour returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts Q and U, the latter from 'chief' on Ukraine, inside QUIDPROO, before its final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid pro quo is a favour or advantage given in exchange for something else.

clue.text: Ulster politicians permitted ally's ultimate betrayal?

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
licit means lawful, permitted

indicators.note: ultimate picks the last letter of ally's

explanation.surface: Asks whether Ulster unionists were finally betrayed by their Conservative allies.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP propped up the May government and felt betrayed by the Brexit deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity is double-dealing deceit, which is what a betrayal involves.

clue.text: Sanchez ultimately in the hands of leaders of independence battle in autonomous Catalan-speaking territory

indicators.note: in the hands of means the end letter is held inside the initials
leaders of takes the first letter of each of the following four words
ultimately picks the final letter of Sanchez

explanation.surface: Spanish prime minister Sánchez is in the hands of an independence struggle in autonomous Catalonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives Z, and 'in the hands of' puts it inside IBIA, the leaders of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza, in the Balearic Islands, is an island where a form of Catalan is spoken.

clue.text: Green fighter in prison?

definitions.meaning: the Incredible ... is the green-skinned superhero of Marvel comics
an old hull of a ship moored and used as a prison

explanation.surface: An environmental campaigner locked up for the cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marvel superhero turns green when angry, and old prison ships were called hulks.

clue.text: Use ride-sharing system? Problem with lift

parts.note: a hitch is a problem or snag
to hike is to lift or raise, as in hiking prices

explanation.surface: A query about using a ride-hailing app, with a glitch in getting a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like a car ride, which suits the definition, but it is a raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitchhike is to travel by getting free rides from passing drivers, a primitive ride share.

clue.text: What Johnson is May to July?

definitions.text: What Johnson is May to July?

parts.words: What Johnson is May to July?
parts.note: Boris Johnson holds the office that Theresa May held until July 2019

explanation.surface: Reads like a question about a change over the months from May to July.
explanation.walkthrough: May and July look like months; May is Theresa May, who left office in July 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Theresa May and Boris Johnson led the UK government as head of the cabinet.

clue.text: Suspend professional prankster

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a rogue is a mischievous rascal or prankster

explanation.surface: A demand to suspend a joker from a professional body.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson's prorogation of Parliament in 2019 was ruled unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue Parliament is to suspend its sittings without dissolving it.

clue.text: Means and what they are said to justify, in support of elected leader of Tories

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in support of others sits below them

parts.note: in means elected, voted into office

indicators.note: the leader of Tories is its first letter

parts.words: what they are said to justify
parts.note: the proverb says the ends justify the means

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek look at an election, the means it uses and the leader they back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' is a verb here, though it looks like the noun in the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to mean it, have it as one's purpose.

clue.text: Exit — die being the alternative?

parts.note: split into two little words, the definition's word opens a saying of grim resolve whose other option is to die

explanation.surface: A grim choice between leaving and dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the way out of a room, an exit.

clue.text: Only domestic produce available here — where can one buy ships?

definitions.meaning: a shop selling home-made handicrafts, goods produced at home
craft also means boats, so read literally it is a store for vessels

explanation.surface: A shopper at a local-produce outlet wonders where they could buy a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop of handmade goods sells homely produce, and craft also means vessels.

clue.text: Follow leader in a merry dance, losing in like 58 seats?

definitions.text: Follow leader in a merry dance

indicators.note: losing means the following letters are dropped from the end

parts.note: in the 2019 election the Conservatives gained 58 seats, each shown on screen as a Con gain

explanation.surface: A party leader leads followers a merry dance while losing many seats.
explanation.walkthrough: CON GAIN was the TV caption for a seat the Conservatives took, 58 times in December 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: In a conga, dancers form a line holding the hips of the one in front and follow the leader.

clue.text: After public relations initiative's launch, November borders on catastrophe for royal

indicators.note: the launch of initiative's is its opening letter

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the borders of catastrophe are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A royal whose PR initiative in November borders on disaster: Prince Andrew's interview.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of a royal family, a king's or queen's son.

clue.text: Northern town with Labour not returned

parts.note: labour means work, so labouring is working

indicators.note: returned means the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A northern seat where Labour was not elected again in 2019.
explanation.walkthrough: Workington, in Cumbria, was won by the Conservatives in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Workington is a town in Cumbria in the north of England.

clue.text: Hong Kong upset by an Asian leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Unrest in Hong Kong distresses an Asian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Khan is a title of rulers in Central Asia, as with Genghis Khan.

clue.text: Lifting toilet takes time, first, and specialist equipment

indicators.note: first means the time letter comes before the rest
in a down clue, lifting means the letters are raised, reading upwards

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Raising a toilet needs time and a plumber's special kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes time, first' means the time letter leads; 'Lifting' reverses the toilet word upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement or instrument used for a specific job.

clue.text: Source of biometric data digital assistant turned over?

indicators.note: turned over means the assistant's name is flipped end to end

parts.note: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled digital assistant

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a voice assistant gave up personal biometric data.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris scans are used, like fingerprints, to identify people by their eye's unique pattern.

clue.text: Conduct unprofitable business in travel, failing to understand

parts.note: to run is to travel, as a bus runs
at a loss means bewildered, unable to understand

explanation.surface: A business is losing money in the travel trade without knowing why.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm running at a loss is spending more than it earns.

clue.text: A head mischief-maker evading charge

indicators.note: evading means the mischief-maker slips out of the charge word

parts.note: to impeach is to charge an official with misconduct
an imp is a small mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A troublesome headteacher avoids being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' means per person, as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Five pounds a head is five pounds for each person, so the two phrases match.
